chapters.title: Chapter 3876: Existence is Unfair V
paragraphs: The golden waters of Paradox held their breath.

Thousands upon thousands of Foldless Ones hovered above and around them, gazes fixed like Omniverses that had forgotten how to blink. Each pair of eyes was sharpened by hunger. By awe. By the pull of something they did not understand, but desperately wanted.
The Honored Ones moved first.
From behind the still figure of the Honored Living Golden Paradox, others began to drift forward- immense beings, draped in flames of authority and halos forged from unspeakable truths.
Their presence alone pressed against the very fabric of this fold, and still... they came.
They were unfathomably powerful.
In this immediate region, only Noah and Aetheron were the only Originus Venerant entities!
All others were in their own glorious stages of power that exceeded 100,000,000 PQ and CQ!
There were Living Paradoxes here, Prime Living Paradoxes, and Honored Living Paradoxes!
All gazing. The Honored Ones coming!
But as they neared the dome of paradox where he remained, Noah began to laugh.
"Haha...Haha!"
A heavy, booming laughter!
It wasn’t a sound born of joy.
It wasn’t mad.
It wasn’t meek.
It was deep and whole, even with most of him gone.

The laugh echoed softly, and yet it rang clear through the hush of the Foldless Ones, through the golden seas, through the lingering sparks of blood and betrayal. It was the sound of something beyond defiance.
Noah’s fractured chest rose slightly with each breath as his head tilted toward the skyspace, his eyes crinkling at the edges with something close to wonder. Or perhaps rage wrapped in silence.
"You’re all correct," he said.
His voice wasn’t loud, but it carried across quintessentially. The golden sea listened. The hungry eyes leaned closer.
"Existence," he whispered, "is unfair."
The words floated magisterially.
He turned slowly, the remains of his body unmoving save for his head, now angled to stare straight through the crowd of Living Paradoxes, especially Diviticus.
"But existence doesn’t discriminate in its unfairness," he murmured. "It may be unfair to me today... but it can be just as unfair to you tomorrow."
The silence afterward was sharp enough to cut halos in half.
He didn’t need to shout. He didn’t need to curse. His words weighed more than power.

Diviticus, unshaken, lifted a hand and waved it once, her expression amused, tinged with pity. "A shame it had to play out this way," she said, tone laced with cruel elegance. "But you were never going to be the center of anything. Not in the eyes of the Paradoxes. You are no chosen who was going to be groomed into a pinnacle figure. Such a thing would hava taken too long. You’re no messiah. You’re a...well. A well filled with waters of possibilities, and we’ll drink deep."
HUUM!
Her gaze flicked toward the Honored Living Golden Paradox and the others now drifting forward, eventually coming to land on Moiraine.

"You see it now, don’t you?" she said, her white flames undulating across Aetheron’s shoulders. "The future doesn’t lie in nurturing one child. It lies in many. Let him go. And with his blood, we’ll grow into the glory we’ve long deserved."
Noah met her stare with an unblinking calm.
"Even if you and all of your fellow Honored Ones devour every drop of my existence," he said, voice low and razor-thin, "you won’t reach half of what I would have become."
His words did not rage.
But they rang out gloriously.
Diviticus scoffed calmly, her head tilting. "Now you’re just speaking nonsense. Your pain has made you poetic."

She shook her head. "Let’s not drag this out. You’ve seen what we’re capable of. You can’t move. You can’t speak much longer. And with Living Paradoxical Authority sealed across the Goldfolds... you are powerless."
She smiled then. It wasn’t kind.
"So why not offer yourself to others with dignity?" she asked. "For your kind. For their salvation. That’s something, isn’t it? To die... with dignity?"
The words lingered.
Noah repeated them slowly. "With dignity..."
He nodded.
Beside him, Moiraine’s form trembled.
Flaming golden paradoxes of cold rage carved trails down her face, burning into the sea of paradox beneath her.
They did not know that he truly was not simply a Paradox that does not produce Inevitabilities!
She had said she would protect him.
She had believed she could.
And now...

Now she could only kneel beside what was left of him as the dome flickered under pressure. As the Honored Ones advanced. As all the Foldless Ones around them began to drift closer, slow and silent like an eclipse in motion.

Noah tilted his head once more, his cold gaze falling across them. The Honored Living Golden Paradox. The six that had surrounded Diviticus. The multitudes beyond them. All of their shapes burned into the void behind his eyes.
"I will remember this," he said. "Every single one of you. I will remember."
Moiraine’s voice boomed calmly as she rose up beside him, "This is not the way. You don’t understand what you’re doing!"
WAA!
But her words were swallowed by silence.
No one answered her.
No one stopped.
They had already made their choice.
And so had he.
At the end of the day, it all came down to choices.
Those damn choices!
Noah’s final words carried not as a plea, but as a curse wrapped in understanding.
"Today... Existence was unfair to me. But I hope... you remember this moment well when it is your turn. When existence becomes unfair for you."
HUUM!
And then...
A soft chime.
Living Paradoxical Authority was not usable under the domain the Honored Living Golden Paradox released.
But he never had just that!
The Glyph on his forehead flared.
Not gold. Not white. Not crimson.
Silver.
A silver glow, faint at first, then blooming like a rising moon beneath the sea.
Living Dimensional Authority.
It shimmered across the dome, across the golden sea, slipping through the silence like a fucking ghost.
The Honored Ones halted mid-flight.
Diviticus’s brows furrowed.
"This..."
But it was too late.
The area around Noah and Moiraine began to fracture with purpose. A soft collapse of folded dimensions, layer by layer, peeling back like paper burning in reverse.
The golden sea rippled once, and then...
POP!
They were gone.
No eruption. No explosion.
Just a breath, and then absence.
Before the tens of thousands of Foldless Ones could even begin to react, there was nothing left where the Young Paradox had stood.
Only a lingering echo of silver, still humming like a lullaby.
And the flicker of choices.
Of causality.
Of consequence.
And there would be...Consequences!

chapters.title: Chapter 3877: The Living That Are Bound! I
paragraphs: The Goldfolds had an unfathomably heavy silence.

In a dominion ruled by the will of the Honored Living Golden Paradox, where golden seas of Paradox stretched out like a glorious commandment, a single truth had always reigned- no Living Paradoxical Authority could be used unless by the Honored Living Golden Paradox himself.
That truth had been a pillar of control, of order and of certainty as this heavy ordeal occured.
And then... Noah disappeared!
The Paradox they wanted to completely devour...disappeared!
Before the eyes of tens of thousands of Foldless Ones.
Before the gazes of Honored Ones who ruled regions of existence with a flick of their will!
He vanished through a burst of silver light- an elegant unraveling of space and direction, the golden paradox sea collapsing around him as if its structure meant nothing.
The stillness that followed was not calm.
BOOM!

It didn’t erupt from any one place. It bloomed in every mind at once- the roaring, collective realization of something they could not yet name. The very air shimmered as voices burst out like cracking glass.
"He vanished...!"
"That was another Authority...!"

The gold sea roiled violently, waves of thick light smashing against each other in erratic ripples. Beings who had lived for endless ages, who had studied the weavings of Living Authority with near-religious rigor, now stared at the impossible with eyes that refused to blink.
And then Honored Diviticus roared coldy.

"That was Living Dimensional Authority!" she bellowed, her white flames dancing wildly around her frame, the scorch of them making even nearby Honored Ones tense. "He can utilize Living Dimensional Authority!"
The words tore through the sea like lightning.
The Foldless Ones recoiled, some shaking their heads in disbelief, others muttering in shock.
No one questioned whether Noah was a Paradox. That had been proven long ago. They felt it. Diviticus also just ate a major part of him, so she knew it.
But a Paradox who could wield another Living Existential Authority?
How?
How could such a thing exist?
How could someone do what should be impossible?
Even Honored Gold, stalwart as ever, wore a face painted in grave realization.
"All Golden Paradoxes under my command," his voice boomed out like a mountain’s heartbeat, "are to set off at once. Track them. Moiraine... and the Existential Anomaly."
That final word echoed with weight.
An anomaly.
Not a title. A declaration.
Because what else could he be?
The moment the command resounded...
BOOM!
The golden sea cracked.
It dried.
As if drained by some glorious hand, it folded into itself in great sheets, splitting like thin parchment. The light dimmed.
The pressure lifted. Then, every single Foldless One in this area- every single Living Paradox that was not an Honored One, froze.
No screams. No shouts. No movement.n(o)v.el.com
Stillness.
Their minds and weavings arrested mid-thought, held in a time-woven stasis that spared no one.
And then, a throne descended from above!

It was composed entirely of Miniaturized Transcendent Wheels of Existence, each spinning with untraceable speed, each emitting a different song of Existence. It hovered in the air above the now-stilled sea, carried by nothing, owned by none!
Seated atop it was a man.
Tyrannical. Regal.

Majesty emanated from his skin, his posture, his breath. His black hair shimmered with gold, his face smooth and unreadable, carved from restraint. Robes of black and deep crimson trimmed with white light adorned him, and above his brow hovered a three-pointed crown etched in the shapes of folded infinities.
It was...
A Royal Living Paradox!
Not merely powerful. Revered.
He was flanked by five Honored Living Paradoxes robed in gold, the sigils of infinity blazing on their chests like brands of glory.
Behind them, a hundred Prime Living Paradoxes stood in silence, their white robes marked with smaller sigils, their halos dimmed in deference.
All of them were still as Diviticus called out!
"Duke Elagabalus."
A simple call of respect that others also followed!
And the Paradox on the throne nodded as he moved.
His fingers lifted in the air, and a shimmer passed through the frozen Foldless Ones like a brushstroke of dawn. In the eyes of each, a golden sheen flickered.
He saw everything.
A thousand lifetimes of vision condensed into a moment.
Then, softly, he tapped the side of his crown.
"A Young Paradox that can use both Living Paradoxical and Living Dimensional Authority..."
His voice was low. Measured.
"Mmm."
He turned his head, gaze falling to the Honored Living Golden Paradox.
"Gold," he said, "Continue as you were and use everything at your disposal. Find them."
A command given like a whisper from a throne. A whisper that moved mountains.

HUUM!

And Diviticus did not freely display it as she sheemed to understand something.
So...
Diviticus bowed low, her mouth curved in something between triumph and quiet hunger.

With a lazy gesture of his hand, Elagabalus rose from his throne as it shimmered, turning translucent, then gone. In an instant, he, his retinue of Honored and Prime Living Paradoxes, and Diviticus disappeared.
Silence returned.
And then...
The Foldless Ones blinked, unaware of their frozen state moments before.
The whispers returned. Confused. Shocked.
But then, another boom of authority echoed out.
The Honored Living Golden Paradox released a pulse of gold that shook the Skyspace once more, commanding silence.
"Oryzarakh," he called out, his voice like the tolling of a bell.
The glorious figure who had stood frozen beside Aetheron now stepped forward. The light on his face was grim.
He thought of Moiraine. The glorious Moiraine! But now...ah!
"There’s an anomaly to find," Honored Gold said. "Let’s begin where he came from."
He turned slowly, the weight of his eyes heavy.
"Let us go to the Folds that Paradox stemmed from."

chapters.title: Chapter 3878: The Living That Are Bound! II
paragraphs: Across the weavings of existence.
Within the Nullvein Gravewake Folds.
BOOM!
Living Dimensional Authority detonated in absolute silence.
It was an elegant annihilation of causality itself. The fractured corpse of a dead Wheel of Existence quaked as Authority more ancient than time swept across it.
Paradoxical gold followed.

A blaze of contradicting frequencies, folded and twisted until they radiated something both glorious and unspoken. Together, the silver and the gold painted a weaving of power that did not belong in this desolate region!
And then, two figures emerged.
One, impossibly still. The other, impossibly shocked.
Moiraine, her body cleaved from the waist down, floated amidst the ruin like a sovereign cast from royal paradox.

Her long white gold hair flowed without wind, her eyes twin golden stars flaring beneath her brow. Cracks laced her skin, yet nothing about her presence seemed weakened. Authority clung to her like a loyal hound.
And in her arms...
Ozymandias, or what was left of him.
A portion of his head, his upper chest- those remained. Everything else had been reduced to raw echoes.
He opened his eyes.
There was no panic within them, only the silent weight of someone who had already decided what came next.
Moiraine’s eyes flared as she looked down upon him.
Her voice was quiet. Too quiet.
"Living Dimensional Authority," she whispered, the syllables trembling. "That was Living Dimensional Authority. You...!"
Noah looked up at her.
Not hurried. Not moved by urgency or spectacle.
Only deliberate.
"There is no time," he said, voice a low current wrapped in certainty. "You have this span of an instant."
The way he said it- this span of an instant- as if time bowed to him, not the other way around.
His gaze met hers.
Unshaken. Quintessential!
"You’ve walked beside me this far. Protected me when it served no gain to do so."
Moiraine said nothing.
She listened.
A true Paradox did not interrupt the unfolding of inevitability.
Noah’s voice did not waver.
"I mean to save you," he said, "but I also require my own assurances."
A slight shift. His words were calm and absolute.
"Accept me. And I will show you what those dogs in the Goldfolds just turned away from with their snouts in the air. You have now- this single moment to decide."
A single moment!
A single instant!
After he said this, he moved.
His forehead came to rest against hers.
Not a movement of affection.
An initiation.
He activated the same ability he once used on Sigrid- the binding force of an Early Creature, one meant to tether Living Existences to himself!
But where Sigrid had been fragmented and lost, Moiraine was whole.
Even damaged, her power was vast.
A cathedral of flame and knowledge. A storm of living contradiction. The kind of being that did not submit!
His aura pressed into her.
And like a thread of silk trying to wrap around a mountain, it faltered.
Small. Honest. Entirely insufficient.
Unless...
Unless the mountain leaned down.
Unless the storm... allowed it.
Moiraine did not rush.
Because this single instant... stretched long within her.
She thought of the Honored Ones.
Of the Council.
Of Diviticus.
Of betrayal wrapped in white fire and honeyed tones.
She thought of how power turned loyalty into hunger. Of how easily the Foldless Ones had shifted with want. With need. With entitlement.
And then... she thought of him.
Noah. Ozymandias.
This anomaly. His words. His actions. Why she truly believed he was the answer and what Diviticus had done was wrong!
She had to decide.
And so, she did!
She folded herself down. Compressed her essence. Let her glory become wrap-able.
She allowed it.
She chose.
BOOM!

A rupture exploded out from the dying Wheel, carrying with it a shockwave of Paradoxical Complexity. It tore through the Gravewake Folds with impossible pressure, searing through layers of silence and ruin.
Prompts burned into Noah’s vision.
|You have successfully bound a second Living Existence under your banner as an Early Creature.|
|You have successfully bound a Living Paradox. Living Paradoxes may now be born within the Festival of Existence and the Early Veiled Shore.|
His gaze flickered, silver light sparking from the hollow of his forehead.
Moiraine exhaled slowly.
Her body trembled beneath the sheer exposure to an Early Creature’s resonance- closer than she’d ever been. Even she, with her eons of sovereignty, had to brace herself.
Noah’s voice was quiet again. It simply pressed downward with finality.
"You are mine now."
WAA!
Moiraine’s head did not bow. But her weavings flickered once in acknowledgment.
And then, both of them vanished!
A nanosecond later.
The Gravewake Folds rumbled again.
HUUM!
A ripple of white and blue bloomed.
From it emerged a massive form, a nine-headed turtle, its carapace glistening with Living Origin Authority that poured off its heads in controlled, solemn swells. Around it, the Gravewake dimmed.
Its many eyes were somber.
They focused on the residue of silver and gold that lingered like fading starlight.
Moments later, Altheon and Shaynara arrived with other Living Origins- each cloaked in silent power, each face cast in veils of caution and shock.
Altheon’s voice came low and steady.
"This aura... belonged to a Living Paradox."
He paused.
"One that is approaching Honored Tier."
He turned to the others.
"Why did they come here? Why did they vanish?"
There were no answers.
Only the frantic spreading of their weavings, an effort to trace a path that no longer existed.
They would not find it.
They never could.
The Early Veiled Shore
The Veiled Shore trembled as a new existence arrived above its radiant sands from a light of Living Dimensional Authority.
Moiraine!
The sands shifted beneath her. Her torso floated upright, flames cascading from her exposed abdomen like a burning veil. Her eyes opened wide.
She had barely acclimated when a hurricane of Living Paradoxical Authority bloomed around her, many magnitudes beyond the Dyson Singularity.
Boundless Authority flooded into her as she rapidly healed, her feet slowly landing to touch the vibrant sand below her!
She stood, battered and magnificent, absorbing the storm as if she had always belonged to it.
And as her eyes rose until they found him.
Noah.
Not the Ozymandias half-dead in the Folds.
But the one who had always been here.

His main body stood on the clear sands, shirtless, upper body etched with glowing white-gold waves of light that pulsed with life. His obsidian pants shimmered with brilliance, his expression unreadable.
But his eyes were seeing a rise of prompts!
|An extremely complex lifeform has entered the Early Veiled Shore. The probability of Rare and Unique Early Living Marine Lifeforms manifesting has increased.|
|Warning: Population Limit of the Early Veiled Shore exceeded. To stabilize equilibrium, progressive waves of Early Living Marine Lifeforms will be drawn until the limit is restored.|

chapters.title: Chapter 3879: The Living That Are Bound! III
paragraphs: The shoreline was quiet, but not for too long as a low hum began.
The Early Veiled Shore shimmered with a newborn tension. The air was impossibly crisp, layered with the weavings of possibility.

Across from him, the form of Moiraine stabilized. Her fractured essence mended rapidly as golden weavings sewed together bone and sinew, muscle and flame. She stood now, no longer a being of damage, but of majesty restored.
The restoration of her lower body didn’t shake her.
What did... was her surroundings.
And even more than that, the words that proceeded to flash right before her eyes!
|You have arrived in the Early Veiled Shore of a consecrated Early Creature.|
|Your Complexity and Purity are rising rapidly.|
Her eyes widened.
But not with confusion. Not even with awe.
Recognition.
Early Creature. Early Veiled Shore!
The words boomed and collapsed many things she thought of!
Early! Creature!
This meant...! This meant...!
Oh!
Now it made sense.
It all made sense!
His aura. His blood. That intoxicating pull beneath his skin.
The ability to wield more than one Living Existential Authority.
He wasn’t a Paradox made to defy tradition.
He was a creature that could control Paradox!
Moiraine looked up at him slowly.
And in her eyes, something changed.
Noah watched this processs play out in motion.

He had always known that eyes were the first liars and the last truth-tellers. Through them, people concealed, and yet they always revealed. A glance carried possibility. A stare carried motive. Eyes never stayed the same over time.
And now, her eyes were different.

Before, they looked at him with purpose. Not compassion. Not control. Just purpose. She saw him as something valuable. As a possibility for the Loom, for eventually attaining her goal of standing before THE Living Paradox.
But now...
Now he saw fear.
Reverence.
Truly. In someone far more powerful than him, he saw reverence and fear!
A foreignness that distanced her from him more than space ever could.
He didn’t want that.
He didn’t need worship.
He needed understanding.
Yet still, she walked forward.
Moiraine’s steps were slow as she dropped to one knee. Her head bowed.
The air did not shift.
She did.
"I greet Sir Early Creature for the first time truly. I-"
"Stop."
Noah’s voice was level and clear.
She froze instantly.
His hand lifted lightly in the air.
"You don’t need to kneel."
Behind him, the others turned at the shift in tone.
Amelia Osmont and Adelaide.
Henry, gazing towards his father with wide eyes.
Further back- Ruination, shimmering with ruinous glory. The Infiniverse, silent and elegant. Liora, cradling a forged glass bucket she had finished forging!
All watched.
Noah looked back down at Moiraine.
"Get up," he said, more softly this time. "You don’t need to change how you speak. Talk to me as you did before you knew anything."
He told her.
And yet...
Moiraine remained where she was.
Unmoved.
The golden light around her flickered once more.
Her voice came quiet, but sure.
"You don’t understand. Early Creatures haven’t been seen in existence for countless eras. Not one."
She raised her face slightly.
"In the Earliest Folds, it was from your kind, born of the Blood of the Creature, that many types of Living Existences came into bloom. To be here before you... is an honor I cannot desecrate."
Her eyes grew solemn.
"And for you to have held me. To have spared me. To have chosen to bind me..."
She lowered her gaze again.
"For what the Living Paradoxes did to your other body..."
The flames behind her surged as her tone tightened.

"I will get retribution with all my existence on your behalf. They made a mistake I warned them of. One they cannot comprehend. And if they knew... if they understood even a fraction of what you were...ah!"

She thought of all that could have been!
An Early Creature had actually come to their Folds!
To the Living Paradoxes!
And they actually made an enemy out of him!
What a colossal fuck up that was.
The golden flames crackled around her shoulders.
Then, she lowered herself further.
Her knees pressed into the soft glow of the shore. Her voice was calm now with no tremble, no hesitation.
"Sir Early Creature. As in the Earliest Folds, I stand as a Living Existence under your disposal. Tell me to act, and I will act. Tell me to kill, and I will kill. Tell me to die...and I will die."
Her eyes lifted once more.
And they were different now.
Not the eyes of Moiraine- the stoic, powerful, enigmatic Paradox of the Foldless Ones.
These eyes of a being with deep reverence and fear of the identity of an Early Creature and what they represented.
Noah stared at them in silence.
He didn’t feel triumph.
He felt loss.
He sighed- long and heavy, letting the breath pull through his chest.
And even more he could reply...
HUUM!
The Early Sacred Waters of the Budding Shore trembled.
They pulsed with layered resonance.
|A Wave of Early Living Marine Lifeforms have risen to rectify the population.|
A moment later, from the heart of the glow, forms emerged.
Early Living Marine Lifeforms!
Eleven.
The first ten- glorious and translucent, carried the Basic Early Living Existential Glyph of Water etched into their flesh. Their scales shimmered with aquatic luster, their bodies sleek and precise.
But the eleventh...
It emerged last, floating without ripples, its gaze level.

Its body was serpentine eel, endless, like a ribbon of liquid diamond. Upon its head burned the Refined Early Living Existential Glyph of Water, far more intricate than the others. Six additional Basic Glyphs pulsed along its body.
|Name: Virellith, the Abyssal Spring Monarch.|
|Type: Early Living Marine Lifeform.|
|Authority Type: Living Water.|
|Refined Early Living Existential Glyph: Water (1).|
|Basic Glyphs: Water (6).|
|Tower of Origin: Living Water Tower of Origin.|
"ROAAAR!"
Its heavy bellow echoed.
Their intent was clear.
Correct the population.
Kill.
Noah stared at them.
A minute ago, the appearance of a single one would have forced retreat. A few minutes more, and they’d have devastated everything here.
But now?
He watched the sky ripple above them as the Sea trembled.
He closed his eyes briefly and thought of Loss.
Loss had its place in existence.
It opened the door.
It tore the ceiling.
It created space.
Sometimes, he thought, loss was the only way to build again. Not as you were before. But as something entirely new.
From broken Towers.
From stolen blood.
He had gained something- Moiraine.
And now...
He looked at the undulating waves beyond, where more Lifeforms stirred.
He didn’t flinch.
He didn’t even look again.
Instead, he turned, walking toward the others as he spoke calmly to the Paradox still kneeling.
"Take care of the marine lifeforms that will keep coming."
He didn’t look back.
"Kill them."
WU!
"But keep their bodies intact."
The instant the command left his lips....
BOOM.
The aura of a terrifying Foldless One erupted in resonance.
It rose like a spear of inevitability.
The incoming Marine Lifeforms paused in their advance as their Existence felt fear!
